poems: Ten sharp. The scaffolding crew has been up since six and is already talking about lunch.

10:01. Eleven tabs open,
one of them playing sound.
A ladder against the gutter. Nobody on it.
Deep focus is a rumor spread by people who do not share a calendar.

Things on the desk:
mug ring,
two pens that work,
a third pen,
the receipt from Tuesday.
The mortar is mixed. Keeping it from setting is now the entire job.
Somewhere a nurse writes 1006 and leaves out the colon, the way she was taught.
At 10:07 the printer decides.
You opened the document. That was the hard part, you tell yourself, knowing better.
Orange cones, a hole, three men looking in.
Ten ten. The digits agree. Nothing else does.
The email nobody wants to answer has sat two days and has not gotten worse.
Sanding. The arm knows how long.
10:13, and the meeting that could have been an email is being an email, in the chat, during the meeting.
Focus, n.: the twenty minutes between the second coffee and the first notification anyone answers.
Quarter past. The hygienist says rinse. You rinse.
Somebody is on hold. The music is a synthesizer imitating a harp, and it has been imitating a harp since 10:04.
Sod on a flatbed, sweating.
The retired man at the bank window is not in a hurry and has never once been wrong about that.
To assemble: align part A with part B. Start every bolt before tightening any. There is always one washer left.
Ten twenty. The mail carrier is on the block with the dogs.
The tile guy has been here four hours and said fourteen words, all of them necessary.

10:22. The document titled FINAL_v2
gets a sibling.
A yellow legal pad, one line written, the pen laid across it.
At the library a toddler is hearing about a caterpillar with a serious appetite.
Court is in session. The docket is a list of Tuesdays that got away from people.
A jackhammer starts. Three floors up a therapist raises her voice slightly and keeps going.
Overheard: 'I'm not saying it's wrong. I'm saying nobody asked for it.'
Half the floor has stopped pretending and is reading about kayaks.
The forklift beeps in reverse, the most direct communication in the building.

Half past. Somebody waters the office plant
beyond its needs.
At 10:31 a woman in aisle six compares two nearly identical cans and takes her time.
A window washer's rig ticks down the glass, floor by floor.

GUEST CHECK
1 coffee, refill
1 english muffin
4.75
a smiley face by the total
You could do the thing in nine minutes. You have spent twenty choosing which nine.
A crane operator eats a sandwich two hundred feet up and is not thinking about it.

A window washer drops past the tenth floor.
Accounting looks up as one.
Ten thirty-seven is a bad minute to start anything and a worse one to stop.
The dryer with the good door has been claimed since nine.
Somewhere a substitute teacher is winning.
Ten forty. Two hours of morning left, which is either plenty or nothing, depending.
The dentist says you have been grinding. You have. You will continue.
Roofers on the south slope, shirts off, radio tuned to a station nobody chose.

CONTENTS UNDER PRESSURE
DO NOT PUNCTURE OR INCINERATE
KEEP FROM CHILDREN
See reverse for first aid

10:44. The morning's ambition
files for an extension.

Quarter to. At physical therapy, a count to ten
repeated until it is true.
The truck backs into the dock. Everyone inside knows by sound what is on it.
A hawk on the light pole above the parking lot, doing what hawks do at 10:47, which is nothing, visibly.
The document is open. So is the news. So is a map of a town you will not move to.
Nail gun. Nail gun. Pause. Nail gun.
Ten of eleven. Nothing new starts now. Nobody wrote that rule down and everybody keeps it.
The dish machine at the diner is ahead of the lunch rush and will not be by noon.
At 10:52 the school hallway is empty and waxed, which is somebody's entire morning.
Two ladders, one truck, no one.
Somebody's mother is on speakerphone in a parking lot, and it is going fine.
Five to. A calendar reminder arrives, politely, about a thing you agreed to in March.
Plumber writes the part number on his hand.
Warehouse air held at whatever temperature the bananas need.
10:58. Two minutes to look busy, which takes more effort than the work would have.

Trades wash their hands twice,
paint in the knuckle lines staying.
